numeric_complexity_contract.reference: replay with plain lists: users as a list of [name, balance] pairs searched linearly, friendships as a list of unordered pairs, pending requests as a list of [sequence, from, to]
numeric_complexity_contract.candidate_design: hash maps for balances and pending requests keyed by sequence number, and a set of canonical friend-pair keys; each request is parsed by splitting on "/"
numeric_complexity_contract.complexity_target: O(total request length) time/O(users + pending requests + friendships) space

numeric_complexity_contract.reference: second-by-second clock: free finished dispensers, seat as many front cars as possible at this second, then advance the clock by one
numeric_complexity_contract.candidate_design: event arithmetic: keep each dispenser's free-at time and remaining fuel; a car starts at max(previous start, earliest free-at among dispensers with enough fuel) and picks the first such dispenser free at that time
numeric_complexity_contract.complexity_target: O(N) time/O(1) extra space

problems.title: Largest K Elements in Sliding Window

numeric_complexity_contract.reference: sort every window afresh and take its first k elements in descending order
numeric_complexity_contract.candidate_design: keep the window as a sorted array, inserting the entering element and removing the leaving one by binary search; read the last k entries backwards
numeric_complexity_contract.complexity_target: O(n * (log w + w_move) + output) time with array moves done by the runtime/O(w) space

numeric_complexity_contract.reference: try every pair of points as opposite corners and look the other two corners up in the point list
numeric_complexity_contract.candidate_design: sort by x and sweep columns; for every pair of y values in a column, remember the first column containing both and score the rectangle from that column to the current one
numeric_complexity_contract.complexity_target: O(n log n + sum over columns of size^2) time/O(n^2) space

numeric_complexity_contract.reference: for every point p and every two other points q and r with (q - p) perpendicular to (r - p), check whether q + r - p is a point
numeric_complexity_contract.candidate_design: group all point pairs by (midpoint sum, squared length): two diagonals in the same group form a rectangle, scored as the absolute cross product of the sides from one corner
numeric_complexity_contract.complexity_target: O(n^2 + sum over groups of size^2) time/O(n^2) space
